Classification of the 18 conformers of the Ag complex by the C2–C1–N3–C4 dihedral.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/ensemble.xyz` — 18 conformers of an Ag complex, 168 atoms (comment line = energy)

**1. Default threshold (90°).**

```bash
frog-sort-ez files/ensemble.xyz -i 2 1 3 4
```

```text

       Dihedral classes
     (files/ensemble.xyz)

│    6 │       -80.11 │ Z     │
│    7 │      -127.16 │ E     │

│   10 │      -126.86 │ E     │

       yz)

╰───────┴───────╯
```

All dihedrals are negative (−133.60° to −34.29°); only $|\phi|$ counts. With the 90° boundary 10
conformers are E and 8 are Z.

**2. Tolerance windows around 0° and 180°, cis/trans labels, and one file per class.**

```bash
frog-sort-ez files/ensemble.xyz -i 2 1 3 4 --tolerance 60 --notation cis-trans -w --out-dir ez
```

```text
…
(files/ensemble.x
       yz)
╭───────┬───────╮
│ Class │ Count │
├───────┼───────┤
│ cis   │     5 │
│ trans │     9 │
│ other │     4 │
╰───────┴───────╯
✔  Saved cis ensemble (5 structures): ez/ensemble_cis.xyz
✔  Saved trans ensemble (9 structures): ez/ensemble_trans.xyz
✔  Saved other ensemble (4 structures): ez/ensemble_other.xyz
```

With windows of ±60° around 0° and 180°, 5 conformers are cis ($|\phi| \le 60°$), 9 trans
($|\phi| \ge 120°$) and 4 other. Two of the *other* conformers, 5 (−119.32°, E above) and 6
(−80.11°, Z above), were forced into a class by the default threshold. The tolerance mode leaves
such intermediate values unclassified. Each non-empty class was written to `ez/`.
